title: Variables and data types
goal: Choose a variable declaration and recognise basic value types.
explanation: Use const when a binding will not be reassigned; use let when reassignment is part of the logic. const does not make the contents of an object immutable.
Strings contain text, numbers represent numeric values, and booleans are true or false. null commonly represents an intentional empty value; undefined often means a value has not been supplied.
Prefer explicit conversion when reading form fields: input values are strings. Check a numeric conversion with Number.isFinite before using it in a calculation.
exercise: Create a name, an age and an isStudent value. Inspect each with typeof.
hint: Use quotes for text but not for numeric arithmetic.

quiz.question: Which declaration allows score to be reassigned?
quiz.explanation: let permits reassignment. const prevents assigning a different value to the binding.
